0|b45b5bd65f668a665db40d093e4e1fe563533608|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"[PATCH] hugepage: Strict page reservation for hugepage inodes
These days
column2: hugepages are demand-allocated at first fault time.  There's a

column1: somewhat dubious (and racy) heuristic when making a new mmap() to check if
there are enough available hugepages to fully satisfy that mapping.
A particularly obvious case where the heuristic breaks down is where a
process maps its hugepages not as a single chunk
individually mmap()ed (or shmat()ed) blocks without touching and
instantiating the pages in between allocations.  In this case the size of
each block is compared against the total number of available hugepages.
It's thus easy for the process to become overcommitted
mapping will succeed
column2: although the total number of hugepages required by

column1: all blocks exceeds the number available.  In particular
a program which will detect a mapping failure and adjust its hugepage usage
downward accordingly.
The patch below addresses this problem
column2: by strictly reserving a number of

column1: physical hugepages for hugepage inodes which have been mapped
instatiated.  MAP_SHARED mappings are thus ""safe"" - they will fail on
mmap()
column2: not later with an OOM SIGKILL.  MAP_PRIVATE mappings can still

column1: trigger an OOM.  (Actually SHARED mappings can technically still OOM
only if the sysadmin explicitly reduces the hugepage pool between mapping
and instantiation)
This patch appears to address the problem at hand - it allows DB2 to start
correctly
column3: which previously suffered the failure described

column1: above.
This patch causes no regressions on the libhugetblfs testsuite
test (designed to catch this problem) pass which previously failed (ppc64
POWER5).
